rationale: The student can segment individual phonemes but struggles to blend them into a whole word. The phoneme-explorer 'blend' mode directly targets auditory blending by having the tutor present separated sounds for the child to blend and pronounce as a complete word.
intent: Practice auditory blending of 3-phoneme short-vowel CVC words. Keep to familiar short-vowel CVC patterns within Grade 1 scope, and exclude the current word 'mat' to ensure genuine practice without giving away the reading task answer directly (e.g., use words like 'sun', 'mop', 'bat'). Provide 3-4 items where the student hears phonemes segmented and says the blended word aloud into the microphone.

data.title: Sound Safari: Reading short-vowel CVC words

judgement.reasoning: The student can isolate phonemes but cannot blend them into a whole word. The detour targets auditory blending (Sound Blend mode in phoneme-explorer) with 3-phoneme CVC words, removing visual text load to practice the essential prerequisite skill. It deliberately omits 'mat' to avoid leaking the current word.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would immediately use this auditory blending detour to help the student combine individual sounds into whole words before returning to print.
